name: Engineered Suppressor tRNA Delivery
therapeuticGoalDescription: Deliver engineered suppressor tRNAs that recognize premature termination codons and insert a near-cognate amino acid, producing full-length functional protein from nonsense-mutant transcripts.
molecularDefect: Nonsense mutations (premature stop codons) that truncate the protein and cause loss of function.
diseaseMechanism: An engineered tRNA with a modified anticodon recognizes a premature stop codon (UAA, UAG, or UGA) and inserts an amino acid (typically tyrosine, serine, or leucine) instead of terminating translation. The ribosome continues translating, producing full-length protein.
typicalDiseases: Cystic fibrosis (nonsense mutations); Duchenne muscular dystrophy (nonsense mutations); other nonsense mutation disorders.
rnaTargetRegion: None. The suppressor tRNA itself is delivered rather than targeting endogenous RNA.
transcriptRequirement: Transcript containing a premature termination codon amenable to suppressor tRNA recognition.
designRules: Design tRNA with anticodon complementary to the target PTC; optimize codon-anticodon interaction for specificity; deliver via AAV or lipid nanoparticle; validate readthrough by Western blot.
secondaryStructureRequirement: Essential. tRNA must fold into correct L-shaped tertiary structure for aminoacylation and ribosome binding.
offTargetConsiderations: Suppression of native stop codons (nonsense suppression); readthrough at normal terminators could produce extended proteins; tRNA copy number and expression level must be carefully controlled.
advantages: Directly rescues full-length protein from nonsense transcripts; leverages endogenous translation machinery; can be specific to a single PTC.
limitations: tRNA delivery is challenging (large molecule); tRNA must be aminoacylated to function; efficiency varies by PTC position and context; risk of global nonsense suppression at high doses; no approved therapies.
clinicalTrialExamples: Preclinical studies in CFTR nonsense mutations; AAV-delivered suppressor tRNAs in mouse models; no clinical-stage programs.

evidenceLevel.note: Proof-of-concept in cell culture and animal models; delivery and specificity challenges remain; no human clinical data.

referencesSummary: UNVERIFIED - see per-reference verificationNote. Floquet et al. (2012); Wang et al. (2017); Lai et al. (2018).

That needs a curated tRNA body per isoacceptor, which is not populated here, and the design is a tRNA rather than an antisense oligonucleotide.
